summary:
On January 8, 2024, at 12:45, Liberty County EMS Rescue 14 was dispatched to the NSK plant for an industrial machinery entrapment involving Jonathan Davis, age 28, whose left arm was crushed by a metal stamping press. A tourniquet was applied by a factory responder and IV Fentanyl 100mcg was administered prior to transport to Midwest Regional Medical Center's trauma unit. At ED triage at 13:28, he was categorized ESI Level 1 (Emergent), with vitals showing BP 88/50, HR 130, RR 24, SpO2 93%, and pain 10/10. He was admitted emergently to ICU-04 at 13:25 under attending Dr. Marcus Vance and admitting Dr. David Cho with a diagnosis of complete traumatic amputation between the shoulder and elbow of the left arm.

Diagnostic workup included X-ray and CT angiography of the left upper extremity, revealing extensive comminuted open segmental fractures of the forearm and hand, a comminuted displaced supracondylar humerus fracture, and complete cessation of contrast enhancement in the brachial artery at the distal third of the humerus, confirming an unsalvageable limb. The emergency physician's impression was a mangled, unsalvageable left upper extremity with complete vascular and neurologic disruption and traumatic shock secondary to acute blood loss and pain. Two units of PRBC were transfused before transfer to the operating room.

Dr. Vance performed an emergent left transhumeral (above-elbow) amputation with myofascial closure, bone beveling, and traction-neurectomy of the median, ulnar, and radial nerves; estimated blood loss was 650 mL, and a JP drain was placed. Postoperative labs showed leukocytosis (WBC 14.2) and anemia (Hgb 8.9, Hct 27.2). Pain management included a Hydromorphone PCA, Gabapentin 300mg, Ancef 1g IV, and PRN Oxycodone. The JP drain was removed on postoperative day 4, and he was discharged after a seven-day admission on Gabapentin 300mg TID, Oxycodone 5mg PRN, and a Cefdinir taper.

At one-month follow-up (2/12/24), he had severe phantom limb pain (8/10) and stump hypersensitivity; Gabapentin was increased to 600mg TID, with referrals for desensitization therapy and shrinker sock fitting. By 6/18/24, a tender 1.5cm neuroma of the ulnar/median nerve stump was identified, prompting a scheduled revision. On 11/12/24, Dr. Vance excised a 1.8 x 1.4 cm neuroma with proximal nerve transposition into the triceps muscle.

Prosthetic authorization was placed on hold in December 2024 pending peer review, delaying therapy until formal PT began 1/12/25. A custom myoelectric transhumeral prosthesis was fitted 2/5/25, followed by ten PT visits through 6/15/26, with two documented no-shows (5/12/25, 11/10/25) attributed to workload and transportation issues. He was discharged 6/22/26 with master-level prosthesis operation, independent ADLs, and clearance for modified light/medium duty work.
